entities.name: Gil Eanes
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Gil Eanes was a 15th-century Portuguese navigator and explorer who played a pivotal role in the Age of Discovery. Born into a family of modest means, Eanes began his maritime career as an apprentice on ships traveling between Portugal and Africa. In 1485, he set sail with King John II of Portugal's fleet to explore the coast of West Africa, becoming the first European to navigate around the Cape of Good Hope in 1488. This remarkable feat marked a turning point in Portuguese expansion and had far-reaching implications for global trade and colonialism. Eanes' legacy extends beyond his navigational achievements, as he also contributed to the development of maritime cartography and the exchange of goods between Europe and Africa. Despite being forgotten by history until recent years, Gil Eanes' name has been rediscovered in scholarly circles, shedding new light on the complexities of 15th-century Portuguese culture.
